_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with an FGFR2 fusion or other rearrangement as detected by an FDA-approved test.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, single-arm trial; patients received pemigatinib 13.5 mg orally once daily for 14 consecutive days followed by 7 days off therapy in 21-day cycles until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with previously treated, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an FGFR2 gene fusion or rearrangement (Cohort A).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Major efficacy outcome measures were overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR) determined by an independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1.
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 36% (95% CI: 27, 45), complete response 2.8%, partial response 33%; median DoR 9.1 months (95% CI: 6.0, 14.5), with 24 (63%) responders having DoR ≥ 6 months and 7 (18%) ≥ 12 months.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 20%) include hyperphosphatemia, alopecia, diarrhea, nail toxicity, fatigue, dysgeusia, nausea, constipation, stomatitis, dry eye, dry mouth, decreased appetite, vomiting, arthralgia, abdominal pain, hypophosphatemia, back pain, and dry skin. Most important serious risks are ocular toxicity (retinal pigment epithelial detachment [RPED] occurred in 6% of 466 patients, Grade 3-4 in 0.6%) and hyperphosphatemia (reported in 92% of 466 patients).
target_moa: Pemigatinib is a small molecule kinase inhibitor that inhibits the kinase activities of FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR3.
companion_dx_detail: Patient selection requires detection of an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement by an FDA-approved test; information on FDA-approved test(s) is available at fda.gov/CompanionDiagnostics.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division did not obtain ODAC advice because no review issues raised significant public health questions regarding the risk:benefit assessment.
